The other great combo is to fly him around with ![](/data/assets/guide/5ecb2adb5abc123f.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fjetpack-cat.png)Jetpack Cat during Tactical Visor.

strengths.title: Consistent damage output
content: Due to his versatile kit, Soldier: 76 is always contributing to a fight. Unlike many other heroes whose value comes in short and infrequent bursts, he never has trouble finding someone to shoot or heal. Whether burning down a barrier, poking with primary fire, or trying to burst an enemy down with Helix Rocket, Soldier’s attacks never cease.

strengths.title: Self sufficient
content: Biotic Field enables Soldier to go on his own solo quests without needing to rely on his team’s resources. A standard gameplay loop looks like run to an off-angle or high ground, Helix and shoot, Biotic Field, shoot, run for health pack, and reposition. All this can be accomplished without ever demanding healing or damage mitigation.

strengths.title: Horizontal mobility
content: As the only hero in Overwatch with infinite ground mobility resource, Soldier’s horizontal mobility is unmatched. He can be very difficult to eliminate because Sprint makes him so evasive. Most enemies have a single charge of their mobility abilities, so Soldier can easily run away.

weaknesses.title: Very long defensive cooldown
content: At 15 seconds, very few Overwatch abilities have a longer cooldown than Biotic Field. Compared to other long cooldowns like Immortality Field and Life Grip, Biotic Field’s defensive capabilities pale in comparison.

weaknesses.title: Master of none
content: Although he has a well-rounded kit, Soldier: 76 isn’t the best hero at any particular function. The snipers out-range him, Sojourn has better burst damage and vertical mobility, Bastion is better at burning down barriers, Tracer is more self-sufficient, and the list goes on.

weaknesses.title: Weak against dive
content: Without any CC or massive burst damage, Soldier is always a dive target. Even though he can Sprint and heal himself, if he gets caught can’t escape, and the healing of Biotic Field is way too low to sustain through a direct attack.

play_against_summary: * Dive him. Every role has heroes who can go with another ally and dive Soldier. He doesn’t have any CC and can’t attack while using his mobility tool.
* Block his poke damage. If all Soldier is doing is shooting barriers, he’s not bringing a lot of value to his team. Either use your own shield or play in the protection of a teammate.
* If you don’t see Soldier in front of you for a while, assume he is about to attack you from your flank. Play near cover so you can escape his surprise attack.

minor.title: Helix Propulsion
content: no guide provided
perk: Helix Propulsion
minor.name: Helix Propulsion
minor.description: Helix Rockets' projectile speed is increased by 50%.

minor.title: Tactical Salvo
content: no guide provided
perk: Tactical Salvo
minor.name: Tactical Salvo
minor.description: During Tactical Visor, Helix Rockets' cooldown is reduced by 80% and no longer interrupts firing Heavy Pulse Rifle.

major.title: Agility Training
content: * When matched up against multiple dive enemies, Agility Training can be the better Major Perk to select. Escaping faster and not having to stop to reload increases uptime without sacrificing evasive maneuvers.
* If Biotic Field is deployed, Sprint around inside it while reloading to keep dodging and healing until reloading has finished.
major.name: Agility Training
major.description: Sprint’s speed is increased by 20% and reload can be performed while sprint is active.

major.title: Stim Pack
content: * Heal or boost

* * Since you don’t lose the option to use Biotic Field for healing if needed, Stim Pack allows for some versatility. Turn Soldier into a glass cannon as he gains attack speed at the cost of being anti-healed.
* The short 4-second window means you’ll want to know and see your target before activating Stim Pack, or else you risk wasting the long CD.
* Cleanse effects

* * Abilities like Protection Suzu, Projected Barrier, and Life Grip will cleanse the anti-heal effect. This is especially good when using Stim Pack for Tac Visor, as the enemy team will likely all turn and focus you.
major.name: Stim Pack
major.description: Stim Pack replaces Biotic Field. On use, Soldier: 76 heals for 30 health per second and gains 20% increased attack speed for 5 seconds.

map_recommendations.maps_summary: The best maps for Sombra have lots of side rooms for her to set up in. Translocator’s versatile movement enables her to access just about any area on any map, so high ground or flat doesn’t matter too much. Sombra struggles on maps with large, open areas that cannot be easily crossed using Translocator and stealth. These areas impede her effectiveness as a flanker. Likewise, if a sightline is too long for her and doesn’t offer enough side paths, she can get sniped during her approach.

play_as: * Translocate first to get into position, stay invisible for the max duration, attack, then immediately Translocate out to stay alive.
* Hack is equally good for initiating a solo attack or for interrupting an enemy attacking your team. Don’t forget to use Hack defensively to help out your allies.

* ![](/data/assets/guide/7fac3c200ab1ed09.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Femp.png)EMP is best used as a combo with another ally’s ult. Check the scoreboard to confirm another offensive ult is available, then wait until that hero is in position to follow up before you EMP.
play_against: * Be on the lookout for Sombra if you haven’t seen her for a while; that means she’s in position to flank you. Be ready to turn around and counterattack.
* If she Translocates right into your team, assume EMP is coming. CC her, dash away, or get to cover.

* Heroes with mobility like ![](/data/assets/guide/2e4a51913793e6dc.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fd-va.png)D.Va and ![](/data/assets/guide/336ae88d165cfe5a.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fanran.png)Anran can chase after Translocate and shoot Sombra out of invis for the kill.
team_comp_synergies: While ![](/data/assets/guide/670bb2169385300d.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fsombra.png)Sombra can be a solo assassin, she's much more effective when paired with at least one other dive hero. Hack-fist is an old term referring to the pairing of ![](/data/assets/guide/b0e3b7fdf5d7ba15.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fdoomfist.png)Doomfist and ![](/data/assets/guide/670bb2169385300d.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fsombra.png)Sombra; a name they earned because of their lethality and the difficulty of countering their set up.
No matter dive hero, the strategy is the same:

1. ![](/data/assets/guide/670bb2169385300d.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fsombra.png)Sombra initiates with ![](/data/assets/guide/c99c013677934a46.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fhack.png)Hack
2. 1. locking the enemy from using abilities

3. The ally (e.g., ![](/data/assets/guide/b0e3b7fdf5d7ba15.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fdoomfist.png)Doomfist, ![](/data/assets/guide/ec8f0896ca78ec6f.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fecho.png)Echo, ![](/data/assets/guide/c5e996565ab1a764.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fgenji.png)Genji) immediately moves in for the kill.

4. ![](/data/assets/guide/670bb2169385300d.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fsombra.png)Sombra and teammates disengage, then repeat on next target.

This strategy works particularly well on heroes who rely on their abilities to counter flanks and dives like ![](/data/assets/guide/3bd1f9f730a6a2ce.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fana.png)Ana with ![](/data/assets/guide/89ddbbfe1fbc9a6c.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fsleep-dart.png)Sleep Dart, ![](/data/assets/guide/90fbc15b3208bec3.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fmizuki.png)Mizuki with ![](/data/assets/guide/61a533467bf9f01d.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fbinding-chain.png)Binding Chain or ![](/data/assets/guide/e57835c9ff2eb7ae.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fcassidy.png)Cassidy with ![](/data/assets/guide/f60c62173ce6fce8.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fflashbang.png)Flashbang.

strengths.title: Invisible annoyance
content: Whether or not Sombra is getting elims, she’s always being disruptive to the enemy. The threat of her existence in a backline requires consent, attention and holding onto resources. Against Tanks, getting Hacked is very disruptive so Tanks hate having to play around Sombra.

strengths.title: Ability lockout
content: Both Hack and EMP briefly prevent affected heroes from using any abilities and stop them if they are channelling an ability. As abilities are the most important aspect of any hero's kit, it goes without saying that being able to do this is very strong. Some heroes are completely shut down by a single Hack.

strengths.title: Backline assassin
content: Sombra’s entire kit is perfectly built for assassinating backlines. Supports or Sniper DPS are easy to sneak up on and will generally not be moving too much, and looking straight ahead. The classic, Hack, Virus, shoot combo from behind makes quick work of these isolated enemies.

weaknesses.title: Low damage
content: Although Sombra can burst down a single target, her overall damage output might be the lowest of any DPS hero. This is partially because she spends so much time out of the fight while invisible and Translocating around. If she’s not Hacking the right target at the right time, she’s holding down her team because her damage certainly won’t be carrying.

weaknesses.title: Limited stealth duration
content: Unlike the Sombra of yesteryear, the current iteration can only remain invisible for a few seconds. This means she has to Translocate close to her desired invis target. Since Translocator has an audio cue, enemies can be alerted to her presence and know she only has a few seconds before her location is revealed.

weaknesses.title: Poor range
content: Sombra is only effective at close-range engagements. Hack’s ranged is only 15 meters, and her gun barely deals any damage at that range anyway. Virus can be shot across the map, but its slow speed gives the enemy plenty of time to dodge or block.

play_against_summary: * Be on the lookout for Sombra if you haven’t seen her for a while; that means she’s in position to flank you. Be ready to turn around and counterattack.
* If she Translocates right into your team, assume EMP is coming. CC her, dash away, or get to cover.

* Heroes with mobility like ![](/data/assets/guide/2e4a51913793e6dc.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fd-va.png)D.Va and ![](/data/assets/guide/336ae88d165cfe5a.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fanran.png)Anran can chase after Translocate and shoot Sombra out of invis for the kill.

minor.title: Encrypted Upload
content: * Extra sneaky
* * Use the extra stealth to Hack an enemy, then reposition when they try and turn to attack you. Only commit to revealing yourself with your attack once they're disoriented trying to find you.
* Infinite Invisibility

* * Encrypted Upload increases stealth’s duration to 7 seconds and Translocator is on a 6-second cooldown. So technically, Sombra can Hack and Translocate repeatedly without ever becoming unstealthed.
* Good for Hacking health packs because you make up for lost time with the increased uptime.
minor.name: Encrypted Upload
minor.description: Hack can be used while invisible, successful hacks increase the duration of stealth by 3 seconds.

minor.title: CTRL ALT ESC
content: * Situational

* * Most of the time, you are engaging with Translocator, so you already have full health, or you’re getting away from the enemy so you’re not in danger of dying. Therefore, you won’t need the self-healing too often.
* Moreover, you can just wait for the universal healing passive to kick in for a similar effect.
* Does decrease down time between engages.
minor.name: CTRL ALT ESC
minor.description: Teleporting with Translocator while below half health initiates passive health regeneration.

major.title: High-Speed Bandwidth
content: * Decent when paired with flankers who frequently use health packs like ![](/data/assets/guide/5c24a105db5a970e.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Ftracer.png)Tracer and ![](/data/assets/guide/2d37d713fbda6bee.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fwrecking-ball.png)Wrecking Ball.
* Come in clutch in the niche situation of dueling near a health pack.
* Often people grab health packs out of combat, so the impact is low.
major.name: High-Speed Bandwidth
major.description: Hacked health packs grant allies 25% movement speed and 50 overhealth for 4 seconds.

major.title: Viral Replication
content: * More ult charge
* * Although not as free or consistent, you can deal high amounts of AoE damage through Viral Replication, which also results in faster EMPs.
* Especially good against closely grouped team comps like brawl comps.
* More lethal ultimates

* * As you'll often be hitting a group of enemies with ![](/data/assets/guide/7fac3c200ab1ed09.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Femp.png)EMP, the follow-up ![](/data/assets/guide/193bfabc2fb3df0f.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fvirus.png)Virus is helpful to your team for converting more elims.
major.name: Viral Replication
major.description: Hitting a hacked enemy with Virus spreads Virus to enemies within 8 meters.

map_recommendations.maps_summary:
The best maps to play ![](/data/assets/guide/85db567c48780d42.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fsymmetra.png)Symmetra on either have enclosed objective areas or funnel both teams into one main choke point. On maps with either of these qualities, ![](/data/assets/guide/6811bc86a1033e85.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fsentry-turret.png)Sentry Turret put in crazy work. The enemy has no other pathing or position options but to walk in and deal with your turrets.
Because of her limited primary fire range, Sym also does better on maps with shorter sight lines and worse on maps with long sight lines. The more open an area is, the more space the enemy team has to play outside of her range and away from her turrets.

play_as: * Against Tanks with barriers, focus their shield with your primary fire to ramp up damage and restore your ammo. Once the barrier is down, walk in and melt everyone.
* Place Turrets behind you to watch your Flank. They’ll autofire and thwart those trying to sneak up on you.

* ![](/data/assets/guide/442047e29c6772ee.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fteleporter.png)Teleporter can be used to get your entire team past an enemy stronghold at choke points. Try to get your team to high ground or natural cover behind the enemy.
play_against: * Shoot the ![](/data/assets/guide/6811bc86a1033e85.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fsentry-turret.png)Sentry Turrets. Don’t be the teammate who walks forward, gets blasted by the turrets, and ignores them. On corners, you can quickly peek and fire before they target you.
* Watch for TP. Her team might end up behind you and wipe your backline. Sym may also use TP to dive an isolated target, so always watch to see if her hands are up in the deploy animation.
* Stay out of her effective range. Primary fire and turrets both have very limited ranges, so most heroes have the advantage against Sym at medium to long range.
team_comp_synergies: ![](/data/assets/guide/85db567c48780d42.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fsymmetra.png)Symmetra has two playstyles. One is to use ![](/data/assets/guide/442047e29c6772ee.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fteleporter.png)Teleporter to flank and turret bomb the backline. The other is to play with the Tank, build charge, then melt everyone. To maximize the safety and consistency of the dive style, she needs at least one other hero who can dive with her (on their own or by using the TP).

To play as a frontliner, she wants her Tank to hold the front so she can safely push up with them (e.g. ![](/data/assets/guide/bfc283f3f5c967de.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Freinhardt.png)Reinhardt, ![](/data/assets/guide/3f791ccf8b419b4a.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Framattra.png)Ramattra, ![](/data/assets/guide/452c9a51fb58d39d.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fjunker-queen.png)Junker Queen). Because she has limited range on her primary fire, she can't stand back and poke, but she also can't push up on her own.

The best aggressive pairings for Supports are ![](/data/assets/guide/3d1103aaa0893433.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Flucio.png)Lúcio for speed or ![](/data/assets/guide/df34545acaf615da.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fbrigitte.png)Brigitte for synergy of similar brawl-hybrid playstyles. Symmetra gives Brigitte much-needed mobility through her TP. The range of Repair Packs and TP is nearly identical as well, which enables Symmetra and her allies to be on opposite ends of the TP from Brigitte and still receive her healing. Anyone who gets TP dived by Brigitte and Symmetra is instantly dead because of their high damage and sustain combo.

strengths.title: Repositioning
content: As the only hero with a Teleporter, Sym enables her entire team to reposition to places that would be impossible without her. Once deployed, the teleportation is instant and can be used both ways. From casual play to pro OWCS, we see game-winning plays made possible by sneaky Teleporter placement.

strengths.title: Area control
content: Sentry Turrets excel at area control because three can be deployed at a time and they inflict a slow debuff on their target. Whether she’s using Turrets to hold a choke, defend the objective area, or patrol her flank, once Sym has set up, it’s difficult to take that space back from her.

strengths.title: High DPS
content: Between a level 3 beam and 3 turrets, Sym can deal a whopping 270 damage per second! Even her orb deals 100 burst damage. When she’s able to keep holding primary fire, Sym destroys her targets.

weaknesses.title: Limited range
content: Although Sym’s right-click has infinite range, she's much more effective within range for her beam. She's not very mobile or tanky, so getting into beam range poses a lot of danger to herself. Typically, she'll have to deal with enemy tanks first, and most of them can run her over.

weaknesses.title: Weak to poke and dive
content: Sym tends to fit best when both comps are running brawl or rush comps. She struggles to keep up with her own team’s mobility if they are running dive heroes. When the enemy runs dive, they have an easier time playing around her turrets and can easily collapse on Sym. Her TP makes her easy to chase for high mobility heroes as she can only go to one of two places. Additionally, poke heroes counter Sym by staying out of her range and outputting more consistent damage.

weaknesses.title: Difficult to coordinate with the team
content: When playing Sym, you may come up with an awesome TP strategy, but actually getting your team to coordinate positioning and timing with you ends up being quite the challenge. Your Tank may not protect you while setting up TP, some allies get left behind, and more often than not, your team has no idea what to do or where to go after taking the TP.

play_against_summary: * Shoot the ![](/data/assets/guide/6811bc86a1033e85.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fsentry-turret.png)Sentry Turrets. Don’t be the teammate who walks forward, gets blasted by the turrets, and ignores them. On corners, you can quickly peek and fire before they target you.
* Watch for TP. Her team might end up behind you and wipe your backline. Sym may also use TP to dive an isolated target, so always watch to see if her hands are up in the deploy animation.
* Stay out of her effective range. Primary fire and turrets both have very limited ranges, so most heroes have the advantage against Sym at medium to long range.

minor.title: Sentry Capacity
content: * Patrol and extra flank angle

* * Sentry Capacity is useful to select when the enemy has been flanking you and giving you trouble. You can place one turret on both sides of you, and still have two more to use as you normally would to attack the enemies in front of you.
* More choke pressure

* * Make a semi-circle around the main choke and watch the enemy team get blasted from every angle. Although they can still destroy them, it takes more time and they’ll have suffered more damage in the process.
**Advanced Teleportation**
* Best Minor Perk
* Why you want the extra TP distance
* * Sym doesn’t have to get so close to her desired TP location, which means her deploy positioning is safer.
* When bypassing choke points, you can get your team farther behind the enemy, which often results in a more advantageous position.
* Better escapes
* * When using TP to disengage, you create even more distance between you and your attackers which gives you a higher chance of surviving.
* Dive deep into the backline
* * When the enemy team has a Sniper sitting way in the back who isn’t dying, TP all the way back to them and take them out.
minor.name: Sentry Capacity
minor.description: Sentry Turret gains an additional charge.

minor.title: Perfect Alignment
content: * Max range
* * At level 3 your beam will gain 3.6 extra meters of range for a total of 15.6 meters.
* Counter brawl and rush
* * Against close range and melee enemies, Perfect Alignment will help you outrange them and be able to attack while taking less damage.
* Paired with a speed boost like Lucio or Juno’s Hyper Ring, Perfect Alignment is even stronger because you can get in close to level up your beam, then back up with the extra range.
minor.name: Perfect Alignment
minor.description: Increase the range of Photon Projector's primary fire by 20%.

major.title: Hovering Barrier
content: no guide provided
perk: Hovering Barrier
major.name: Hovering Barrier
major.description: Teleporter gains the option to create a forward moving barrier instead. Pressing Ability 2 again slows down the barrier's movement.

major.title: Shield Battery
content: * Best for duels and flanks
* * If you find yourself spending more time flanking and 1v1ing the enemy than you do on the frontline, then Shield Battery is the better Major Perk for you.
* Receiving constant self-healing comes in clutch to win more duels and flank more aggressively.
* The tether visually indicates you’re in range and receiving healing.
* Refer to _“Tips for Teleporter”_ for a breakdown of offensive strategies to employ with TP.
major.name: Shield Battery
major.description: Symmetra regenerates 20 shields per second while within 10 meters of her teleporter.

map_recommendations.maps_summary:
Torbjörn and his Turrets do best on maps that favor close-range engagements and have choke points that are difficult to break through. When he can set up his Turret behind his team in a position where the enemy team has to walk through a choke to see, it is much harder for them to deal with the Turret. The bullet drop and slow speed of his primary fire put him at a major disadvantage against other ranged heroes on maps with long sight lines.
Although he has decent movement speed from Overload, Torb doesn’t have any vertical mobility. He can deal with the dive comps that traditionally do well on high ground maps, but it's easy for him to fall behind in rotations.

play_as: * Protect your backline with Turret by setting it up in corners behind your team.
* Instead of activating Overload just for extra damage, treat it as a counterattack. Surviving the enemy's attack is more important than desperately trying to get one elim.
* Save Molten Core for when the fight is centered on the objective. Force them off the point or burn them up.
play_against: * Break his Turret first. Try quickly peeking around corners and hiding between your own shots to minimize the Turret's damage.
* Bait out Overload. Soft engage without committing all your long cooldowns, then back up when he’s using Overload. It only lasts five seconds, and you can attack again as soon as it ends.
* Play ranged heroes. Torb is weaker against heroes with range because they can break his Turret from safety and have more consistent damage than his primary fire.
team_comp_synergies: ![](/data/assets/guide/954ef74e420324bc.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Ftorbjorn.png)Torbjörn is a great backline protector when he sets up ![](/data/assets/guide/5a281b66a6179e54.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fdeploy-turret.png)Deploy Turret behind his Supports. Supports like ![](/data/assets/guide/3bd1f9f730a6a2ce.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fana.png)Ana, ![](/data/assets/guide/d61f1a6f760500a9.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fzenyatta.png)Zenyatta and ![](/data/assets/guide/90fbc15b3208bec3.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fmizuki.png)Mizuki who bring high value to your team, but also struggle against flankers are good choices.

For the same reason, sniper DPS also pair well and have the added benefit of making up for Torb's ranged weakness (e.g., ![](/data/assets/guide/62383b6520e2bec1.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fwidowmaker.png)Widowmaker, ![](/data/assets/guide/1745f43a104480df.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fashe.png)Ashe. ![](/data/assets/guide/0df66e1c25a77a79.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fsojourn.png)Sojourn)

For Tanks, he can play fine with dive since he doesn't need a frontline Tank to protect or peel for him (e.g.,![](/data/assets/guide/55b5862f0bee17fa.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fwinston.png)Winston, ![](/data/assets/guide/2d37d713fbda6bee.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fwrecking-ball.png)Wrecking Ball) . However, in brawl and rush (e.g., ![](/data/assets/guide/452c9a51fb58d39d.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fjunker-queen.png)Junker Queen, ![](/data/assets/guide/530a84fb4af55362.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fzarya.png)Zarya) he can use ![](/data/assets/guide/02335ee8dc146b90.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Foverload.png)Overload to go aggro with them and his shotguns melts at close range.

strengths.title: Area control
content: Torb is easily the best DPS hero for controlling space angles and map areas. Turret Auto fires on anybody who enters its LoS, Overload gives him the sustain and damage to contest the enemy, and Molten Core literally turns the floor into lava. When Torb has the chance to set up before the enemy team arrives at a location, he is very challenging to take out.

strengths.title: Self-sustaining
content: With armor higher than average health and the ability to heal himself with overhealth every 10 seconds, Torb doesn't need to rely on his team to keep himself alive. Additionally, his Turret protects him and can be used as a shield if needed. Position near a mega health pack and you’ll be set for life.

strengths.title: Anti-dive
content: Turret and Overload are incredible offensive tools to counter dive heroes. Most other heroes try to deal with dive by escaping, but Torb deals with dive by killing them before they can kill him.

weaknesses.title: Bullet drop
content: Rivet Gun has the worst bullet drop and projectile speed of any weapon in the DPS roster. At medium to long ranges, this makes aiming difficult and hitting shots inconsistent.

weaknesses.title: Situational ult
content: Torb’s ult won’t always get you insane value. Anytime the enemy has fliers or high mobility heroes, Molten Core’s potential goes way down, as they can easily avoid the affected areas. It’s also not an ult you can just click and get kills with, like many other DPS ults are.

weaknesses.title: Weaker on attack
content: While he’s one of the best defenders, Torb can struggle to get set up when he’s attacking. If the enemy team already controls the objective or its his team’s turn to push the payload, he doesn’t have time to set up crossfire with his Turret before attacking. Overall, Torb is better at keeping space than he is at taking it.

play_against_summary: * Break his Turret first. Try quickly peeking around corners and hiding between your own shots to minimize the Turret's damage.
* Bait out Overload. Soft engage without committing all your long cooldowns, then back up when he’s using Overload. It only lasts five seconds, and you can attack again as soon as it ends.
* Play ranged heroes. Torb is weaker against heroes with range because they can break his Turret from safety and have more consistent damage than his primary fire.

minor.title: Hammer Time
content: **Craftsman**
* Niche Perk, but pairs ok with Overloaded Turret Major Perk
* * Extra healing for the Turret can be useful, but then you're also only going to benefit when babysitting your Turret. So this Perk is wasted when paired with Anchor Bolts, for example.
* Focus on holding one area and keeping your Turret healthy, even if you have to body block incoming damage.
* Don’t try to force armor healing
* * Torb shouldn’t be wasting his time trying to heal his allies' armor health. It would be more helpful in most scenarios if he just shot the enemy.
minor.name: Hammer Time
minor.description: Move 20% faster while Forge Hammer is equipped.

minor.title: Pre-Heated
content: no guide provided
perk: Pre-Heated
minor.name: Pre-Heated
minor.description: Molten Core activates Overload.

major.title: Anchor Bolts
content: * Best Major Perk
* High and inconvenient
* * Find places that are way out of the enemy's LoS where they have to look away from your team in order to shoot the Turret.
* Above and behind

* * No enemy is going to be looking above and behind them as they walk through a choke point. Sticking your Turret to the choke point wall won’t shoot the enemy until they come through the choke. But that also means they can’t destroy before walking in.
* New locations
* * When running Anchor Bolts, never just stick your Turret to the floor. Keep changing the location and keep the enemy guessing.
major.name: Anchor Bolts
major.description: Deploy Turret's throw range is increased by 50% and it can now attach to walls and ceilings.

major.title: Overloaded Turret
content: * Decent Major Perk
* Overload damage
* * When Torb activates Overload, and this Major Perk causes the Turret to transform into the Overloaded Turret, there is a notable startup animation before the Turret starts firing again.

* Consequently, you don’t even get the extra damage throughout your whole Overload. So, while this Perk can be helpful because of some extra burst damage, it’s very brief and infrequent due to Overload’s cooldown.
* Instant Turret heal
* * The best part of this perk is really the extra Turret health to keep it alive when it's being attacked. You can Overload, run to Turret with Craftsman, and it becomes very tanky.
major.name: Overloaded Turret
major.description: Overload upgrades your Turret for 5 seconds, increasing its health and damage.

map_recommendations.maps_summary: Tracer’s mobility allows her to find value on virtually every map. The best maps for Tracer, however, are flat maps with plenty of side rooms for flanking. When Tracer can abuse corners and side routes with health packs, her job of being a backline assassin becomes considerably easier. Because she lacks vertical mobility, she can have trouble on maps with lots of high ground that the enemy can use to avoid her. On wide open maps with long sight lines, Tracer wastes a lot of time pathing to avoid enemies with superior range.

play_as: * Dive the backline. The number one job of every Tracer is to either kill or distract the enemy backline. Even if the Supports live, they can’t heal the rest of their team if they're trying to fight you.
* Avoid Tanks. Most Tanks have armor, which negates a lot of your damage anyway. Tracer can annoy Tanks, but she’s wasting her time if she is focusing on them.

* Don’t go in without ![](/data/assets/guide/59884f41423190cf.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Frecall.png)Recall or two ![](/data/assets/guide/2c47faa18b7d4066.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fblink.png)Blinks. Tracer can’t survive fights without the ability to dodge and rewind time. Waiting a few extra seconds for your cooldowns is far better than going in and getting sent back to spawn.
play_against: * Keep your distance. Tracer has terrible ranged damage so try to position where it's difficult for her to reach you, or use mobility tools to dodge her.

* Track ![](/data/assets/guide/59884f41423190cf.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Frecall.png)Recall. You can get used to the timing of Recall to predict where she will rewind to. If you see Recall used, that is your chance to chase and eliminate Tracer.

* If you see Tracer multi-Blink straight at you, expect a ![](/data/assets/guide/4179aa31d749fae6.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fpulse-bomb.png)Pulse Bomb. Use a barrier, stun, or escape tool to avoid getting stuck.
team_comp_synergies: ![](/data/assets/guide/5c24a105db5a970e.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Ftracer.png)Tracer can do everything she's meant to do all on her own. She doesn't need a specific team comp to function. That said, however, dive comps are where she can shine the brightest.

A coordinated dive with another DPS or Tank makes her flanks extremely lethal. Also, having another hero in the enemy backlines with her takes attention off of her and makes her actions safer. Dive Tanks like ![](/data/assets/guide/55b5862f0bee17fa.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fwinston.png)Winston or ![](/data/assets/guide/2e4a51913793e6dc.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fd-va.png)D.Va, and dive DPS like ![](/data/assets/guide/c5e996565ab1a764.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fgenji.png)Genji or ![](/data/assets/guide/52c34367e459b0af.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fvendetta.png)Vendetta, are good choices as they and Tracer can keep up with each other's mobility.

Passive Support healing like ![](/data/assets/guide/495517d449a60604.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Forb-of-harmony.png)Orb of Harmony and ![](/data/assets/guide/e2ee1807aea9c23a.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Frestorative-stream.png)Restorative Stream are really strong for ![](/data/assets/guide/5c24a105db5a970e.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Ftracer.png)Tracer since she can zip around while healing. Her HP is very small, so the light healing brings higher value on her than the huge HP of a Tank.

strengths.title: Self-reliant
content: Tracer can heal herself and use her mobility to grab health packs when needed. At very close ranges, she can one-clip enemy backlines without having to coordinate a dive attack. Unlike most heroes, she can pretty much ignore what her team is doing and execute her own game plan.

strengths.title: Evasive and mobile
content: Her small body and fast movement make her difficult to hit. She can reliably dodge enemy cooldowns and Ults with Blinks and Recall. She’s also one of the best overtime stallers in the DPS category because she gets back to point quickly, then touches, evades, and touches again to keep resetting the OT timer.

strengths.title: Nuisance
content: The hardest part about dealing with a skilled Tracer is that she is always being a nuisance. You can never fully ignore her, but it often feels impossible to kill her. She can single-handedly keep both enemy Supports preoccupied, while her team kills everyone else.

weaknesses.title: Short range only
content: The main downside of Tracer's kit is the limited effective range of Pulse Pistols. Unless you can get close to your target, your damage will barely tickle the enemy. Wide bullet spread and harsh damage falloff prevent Tracer from dealing meaningful damage at medium to long ranges.

weaknesses.title: Mechanically demanding
content: One reason Tracer has always been a staple in pro and top 500 meta, even when she’s been weak in regular ranked play, is that she has a high skill floor and ceiling. Tracking and Blink mechanics make or break good Tracer mains. Even if you execute a perfect strategy, it won’t matter if you can’t land your shots, get lost while Blinking, or whiff Pulse Bomb.

weaknesses.title: Low health
content: Winning the award for lowest health of any hero, Tracer relies on movement to stay alive. She gets insta-killed by a lot of attacks and combos that every other hero would survive. You have to play extra carefully when using Tracer, as small amounts of spam damage quickly deplete her small health pool.

play_against_summary: * Keep your distance. Tracer has terrible ranged damage so try to position where it's difficult for her to reach you, or use mobility tools to dodge her.

* Track ![](/data/assets/guide/59884f41423190cf.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Frecall.png)Recall. You can get used to the timing of Recall to predict where she will rewind to. If you see Recall used, that is your chance to chase and eliminate Tracer.

* If you see Tracer multi-Blink straight at you, expect a ![](/data/assets/guide/4179aa31d749fae6.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fpulse-bomb.png)Pulse Bomb. Use a barrier, stun, or escape tool to avoid getting stuck.

minor.title: Chronal Dash
content: * Increased movement, and can be good for chasing enemies with high mobillity.
* The main problem is that you would have to adjust muscle memory of blink distance mid-round.
* Not worth taking over Kinetic Reload.
minor.name: Chronal Dash
minor.description: Blink distance increased by 20%.

minor.title: Kinetic Reload
content: * Recommended Minor Perk
* Incredibly strong Perk to help secure elims. You literally restore 50% of your ammo with each Melee.
* Blink > Melee when you need just a few more bullets for the kill, as quick melee is faster than reloading.
minor.name: Kinetic Reload
minor.description: Melee hits grant 20 ammo.

major.title: Blink Packs
content: * Considering ![](/data/assets/guide/5c24a105db5a970e.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Ftracer.png)Tracer uses frequently grabs health packs, this will help you get back into the fight a bit faster, multiple times per game.
* Great when dueling and are able to grab a health pack. Tracer puts herself in a lot of 1v1 scenarios. Health packs restoring a Blink give her increased survivability.
* * Also, she can now steal health packs from the enemy **even when she’s at full health**. Don’t let them grab it!
major.name: Blink Packs
major.description: Health Packs restore 1 Blink charge.

major.title: Quantum Entanglement
content: * Helpful for confirming elims
* * Sometimes, enemies survive with a bit of health. Overhealth and extra ammo come in handy to help stay in the fight after Recalling to get that final blow.
* Should probably still disengage
* * Even with the overhealth, if you have no Blinks available, you should still get out of the fight and wait for your cooldowns to refresh.

* In General, don't go aggro after using ![](/data/assets/guide/59884f41423190cf.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Frecall.png)Recall.
major.name: Quantum Entanglement
major.description: Recall grants 50 overhealth and 20 ammo that decays over time.

play_as: * Use ![](/data/assets/guide/1c1049853f308bf0.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fburrow.png)Burrow and ![](/data/assets/guide/f83edd45b5d018be.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fdrill-dash.png)Drill Dash to close into melee range, since ![](/data/assets/guide/47ceb39c2ed21da9.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fventure.png)Venture excels at close-quarters flanks and burst combos rather than long-range poke.

* Manage your temporary shields from ![](/data/assets/guide/34808702edc730f3.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fexplosive-resolve.png)Explosive Resolve by spacing out ability usage so you stay long enough to disengage.

* ![](/data/assets/guide/4a3281f9d6d86612.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Ftectonic-shock.png)Tectonic Shock is best used against heroes without vertical mobility as they struggle to escape the large ground pulses.
play_against: * Venture can still be damaged after activating Burrow until their entire body is fully submerged. Don't let them get away!

* Make a mental note if you don't see ![](/data/assets/guide/47ceb39c2ed21da9.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fventure.png)Venture on your screen. They are likely setting up a flank attack, so be ready to counter.

* When they miss abilities, or you see them use ![](/data/assets/guide/f83edd45b5d018be.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fdrill-dash.png)Drill Dash and ![](/data/assets/guide/1c1049853f308bf0.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fburrow.png)Burrow, that's your signal to hard-focus them at their most vulnerable.
specific_counters_81: ![](/data/assets/guide/b0e3b7fdf5d7ba15.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fdoomfist.png)Doomfist

* Doomfist’s mobility outclasses Venture’s and allows him to hunt Venture down where they would normally be safe. Rocket Punch cancels Burrow and guarantees death. The multiple burst damage abilities of Venture also gives easy charge to Doomfist for his Empowered Punch.
![](/data/assets/guide/e57835c9ff2eb7ae.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fcassidy.png)Cassidy
* Magnetic Grenade. Even if you have horrible aim with Cassidy, all you need to do is stick them with a Magnetic Grenade and your team can easily follow up with enough damage to elim her.
![](/data/assets/guide/3bd1f9f730a6a2ce.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fana.png)Ana

* Similar to Magnetic Grenade, Sleep Dart hard counters Venture’s game plan and abilities. The brief moment of slow movement and vulnerability during the startup frames of Burrow is the easiest opportunity for Ana land a sleep.
team_comp_synergies: Venture works best in Brawl Comps that can utilize their close range damage.
**Ideal team comp built around Venture:**

![](/data/assets/guide/e958e5cf8ba983fa.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fmauga.png)Mauga, ![](/data/assets/guide/47ceb39c2ed21da9.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fventure.png)Venture, ![](/data/assets/guide/e57835c9ff2eb7ae.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fcassidy.png)Cassidy, ![](/data/assets/guide/ca4458a60a9fff01.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fkiriko.png)Kiriko, ![](/data/assets/guide/41367de8021167d5.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Flifeweaver.png)Lifeweaver

strengths.title: Deep flanks
content: The shields generated by Explorer’s Resolve make Venture tanky enough to sustain focused damage on their own. Depending on the situation, Burrow and Drill Dash are interchangeable as engage/disengage abilities. Venture can use these abilities to position themselves behind the enemy backline. Once their cooldowns are back up, they can then go for an assassination. After flanking the enemy back line, Venture can escape over walls with Drill Dash or use Burrow’s invincibility to get out safely.

strengths.title: Burst damage
content: Primary fire, Burrow, and Tectonic Shock all provide great burst damage to players. Burst damage is even more important to OW heroes since the Armor rework in season 10. Moreover, many of Venture's abilities are cancellable into one another, enabling them to deal even faster and larger bursts of damage. (See combos under Tips and Tricks)

strengths.title: Disruption
content: Unlike many other heroes, Venture doesn’t have to get eliminations to be valuable for their team. When the enemy back line gets booped vertically by a Burrowed-Drill Dash, they have to keep an eye on Venture for an additional 4 seconds before they emerge. The time, focus and abilities dedicated to stopping Venture’s assassination is already extremely valuable. The crowd control from both Drill Dash can also disrupt enemy movement abilities and save Venture’s team from elimination.

weaknesses.title: Only useful at extremely close range
content: Venture’s primary fire is a slow moving projectile that can be difficult to direct impact at its max range of 16m. Their other three abilities have to be near melee range to deal damage at all. When against an enemy comp with lots of poke damage, Venture struggles to get in close enough to do damage and isn’t adding any value to their team until they do so.

weaknesses.title: Easily countered
content: Although Venture can be a very good flank hero, they are also easily and heavily countered. Burrow’s long cast animation doesn’t grant invulnerability until completely submerged. CC abilities like Sleep Dart and Magnetic Grenade basically make Burrow unusable as an escape ability.

weaknesses.title: All or nothing
content: Because Venture’s best damaging abilities are also their escape abilities, Venture often has to go in and use every resource to secure an elimination, leaving them completely vulnerable to a counterattack. Venture caught without either Burrow or Drill Dash is a sitting duck and has no counter play if focused by the enemy team.

play_against_summary: * Venture can still be damaged after activating Burrow until their entire body is fully submerged. Don't let them get away!

* Make a mental note if you don't see ![](/data/assets/guide/47ceb39c2ed21da9.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fventure.png)Venture on your screen. They are likely setting up a flank attack, so be ready to counter.

* When they miss abilities, or you see them use ![](/data/assets/guide/f83edd45b5d018be.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fdrill-dash.png)Drill Dash and ![](/data/assets/guide/1c1049853f308bf0.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fburrow.png)Burrow, that's your signal to hard-focus them at their most vulnerable.

minor.title: Deep Burrow
content: * Good for flanks and increasing overall mobility.
* Enables more efficient engages and disengages.

minor.description: Drill Dash distance is 50% longer while while burrowing.

minor.title: Excavation Exhilaration
content: * You dump all your cooldowns to get in and weaken enemies, pop ult, and quickly get them all back.
* The best part is you can burrow into Ult and then again to escape.
minor.name: Excavation Exhilaration
minor.description: While Tectonic Shock is active, cooldowns refresh 300% faster.

major.title: Smart Extender
content: * Really good to give yourself some poke potential.
* Best use is to finish off elims on targets who escape your range mid-fight.
* Though brief, it’s nice to have an option for better ranged damage.
major.name: Smart Extender
major.description: Empower SMART Excavator with E to increase its maximum projectile range by 100% for 4 seconds.

major.title: Covered in Dirt
content: * Best for general flank and close-range combat playstyle that Venture primarily sticks to. Makes them more tanky during fights.
major.name: Covered in Dirt

map_recommendations.maps_summary:
The best maps for ![](/data/assets/guide/62383b6520e2bec1.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fwidowmaker.png)Widowmaker have long-sight lines where she can take advantage of her superior range. She also benefits from high ground she can ![](/data/assets/guide/abe4440fcbb0df97.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fgrappling-hook.png)Grappling Hook up to, then use for attack angles and protection. Maps with enclosed objective areas are difficult for her because she’s forced to play in suboptimal close ranges.
Furthermore, if the map has a lot of side routes for flankers, Widow is vulnerable from too many angles to manage or put ![](/data/assets/guide/be9f23a26307e96b.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fvenom-mine.png)Venom Mines on, so she can’t properly defend herself.
**Best Maps**
* Circuit Royal
* Havana
* Junker Town
* * First Point

play_as: * Hold long sightlines. Widow is at her strongest when she positions outside everyone else’s effective range, where she can still one-shot.
* Reposition frequently after shots. Don’t stay in one spot for long because the enemy will flank you and take you out.
* Prioritize pressure and picks over raw damage numbers. Don’t worry about total damage on the scoreboard. The only thing that matters is shutting down the enemy team, and getting solo kills.
play_against: * Force her to retreat with dives and flanks. Even if you don’t get the kill, stop her from aiming at your teammates.
* Never peek the same angle twice. If you see Widow aiming down sights, don’t walk out at the same position because she will be ready to hit the shot.
* Avoid her sightlines. Scout or get info from your team about her position. Then take side routes where she can’t snipe you.
team_comp_synergies: The first helpful teammate ![](/data/assets/guide/62383b6520e2bec1.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fwidowmaker.png)Widowmaker can have are barrier Tanks like ![](/data/assets/guide/b07e1a5d33e34f21.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fsigma.png)Sigma and ![](/data/assets/guide/bfc283f3f5c967de.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Freinhardt.png)Reinhardt. She makes good use of barriers by standing behind their cover and sniping without fear of getting picked off herself. This also benefits the Tank because the threat of getting one-shot by Widow reduces pressure on their barrier as well.

Another helpful archetype are heores with strong coutner-dive kits such as ![](/data/assets/guide/954ef74e420324bc.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Ftorbjorn.png)Torbjörn or ![](/data/assets/guide/3d1103aaa0893433.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Flucio.png)Lúcio who can peel for Widow. Anyone who can can CC or put high damage pressure on flankers and dive enemies will increase her odds of surviving, even if she's already used ![](/data/assets/guide/abe4440fcbb0df97.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fgrappling-hook.png)Grappling Hook.

Overall, Widow should be taking very little damage, so the only Supports that are directly beneficial are those with a way to enhance her such as ![](/data/assets/guide/c7d7f2bfb765e77e.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fmercy.png)Mercy with damage boost.

strengths.title: Instant oneshots
content: Widowmaker can delete squishy heroes with a single fully charged headshot, instantly giving her team the numbers advantage. At that point, her team will generally win the 5v4.

strengths.title: Lane control
content: Her presence alone denies open areas and long hallways. This forces enemies to take slower side routes, rely on barriers, or burn mobility cooldowns.

strengths.title: Solo carry potential
content: If you are cracked and think your team is holding you back, there is no better solo carry than Widowmaker. The better your aim, positioning, and target selection, the more oppressive she becomes.

weaknesses.title: Feast or famine
content: You either click heads and win, or miss shots and lose. There’s not really an in-between. Widow offers little consistent damage compared to other DPS if she isn’t deleting full HP squishies.

weaknesses.title: Highly vulnerable to dive
content: Grappling Hook is on a 10-second cooldown, which is longer than most dive heroes' mobility cooldowns. Even if she escapes their initial attack, they can chase after her and get the kill before she has another Grappling Hook.

weaknesses.title: Underwhelming DPS Ult
content: Wall hacks aren’t a bad Ult for a sniper hero to have, and it does force the enemy team to position extremely cautiously for its duration. However, compared to other DPS Ults like Sojourn’s Overclock, it’s not exactly a win-button.

play_against_summary: * Force her to retreat with dives and flanks. Even if you don’t get the kill, stop her from aiming at your teammates.
* Never peek the same angle twice. If you see Widow aiming down sights, don’t walk out at the same position because she will be ready to hit the shot.
* Avoid her sightlines. Scout or get info from your team about her position. Then take side routes where she can’t snipe you.

minor.title: Scoped Efficiency
content: * Less downtime thanks to less reloading.
minor.name: Scoped Efficiency
minor.description: Scoped shots cost 3 ammo instead of 5.

minor.title: Sniper's Instinct
content: * Really good in Widow duels or when facing enemies that require you to use grapple to simultaneously evade and attack.
minor.name: Sniper's Instinct
minor.description: Scoped shots charge 100% faster for 2 seconds after using Grappling Hook.

major.title: Widow's Bite
content: no guide provided
perk: Widow's Bite
major.name: Widow's Bite
major.description: Scoped shots can charge up to 125%, piercing enemies when fully charged.

major.title: Seeker Mine
content: * Patrols a much larger area than the standard mine. You’ll be alerted by the 10m radius and can leave it there without having to use the cooldown to redeploy.
**Widow's Bite**
* The charge rate is the same. Charging to 125% takes longer and decreases the rate of fire.
* Enables oneshots on all DPS, including Bastion and Torb.
* Also good if you’re spending more time shooting Tanks.
* The piercing helps on long flat areas a bit, but don’t waste your time fishing for collats.
major.name: Seeker Mine
major.description: Venom Mine now fires poison darts at enemies within 10 meters and remains active after triggered.

map_recommendations.maps_summary:
The best maps for ![](/data/assets/guide/55b5862f0bee17fa.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fwinston.png)Winston have structures, high ground, and plenty of natural cover. ![](/data/assets/guide/55b5862f0bee17fa.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fwinston.png)Winston doesn’t want to have to rely on his ![](/data/assets/guide/3320e3b9cbd5d84c.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fbarrier-projector.png)Barrier Projector as his only means of staying alive. Instead, he performs best when the map’s environment offers protection. Jumping the high ground to push enemies off is his bread and butter. High ground also allows ![](/data/assets/guide/55b5862f0bee17fa.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fwinston.png)Winston to stage dives and drop down on the enemy without having to use ![](/data/assets/guide/71e72edd3dddab12.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fjump-pack.png)Jump Pack. That way, he can leap away at a moment's notice.
The maps Monke struggles on are the wide-open ones with very little cover. Also maps that favor close-range fights on the objective are pretty miserable for him since he has a harder time staying away from his bad matchups.

play_as: * Avoid Tank battles. ![](/data/assets/guide/55b5862f0bee17fa.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fwinston.png)Winston will lose a 1v1 duel against every other Tank. Stay away from them.

* Don’t sit at the choke point. Short range and minimal damage mitigation make ![](/data/assets/guide/55b5862f0bee17fa.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fwinston.png)Winston bad at contesting choke points. Use Leap to bypass chokes and get to flank angles or high ground.

* Look for isolated dive targets. Anytime you see an enemy a bit separated from their team, ![](/data/assets/guide/71e72edd3dddab12.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fjump-pack.png)Jump Pack onto them and try to get a quick elim.
play_against: * Track his cooldowns. When ![](/data/assets/guide/55b5862f0bee17fa.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fwinston.png)Winston uses either bubble or leap, his enemies have a generous window to target him where he can’t shield or jump away. Focus him when he can’t escape.

* Keep your distance. Most heroes have CC to stop or knockback ![](/data/assets/guide/55b5862f0bee17fa.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fwinston.png)Winston, or a movement ability to run away. Try to never let him get close to you, as he’s only a threat up close.

* Stay in an ally Support’s LoS. ![](/data/assets/guide/55b5862f0bee17fa.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fwinston.png)Winston's damage is rather low, and most Supports can keep you alive with their healing even while he’s attacking you. Eventually, you’ll do more damage than him, and he’ll have to disengage.
team_comp_synergies: ![](/data/assets/guide/55b5862f0bee17fa.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fwinston.png)Winston doesn't have lethal burst damage on his own. If his target is receiving healing, he generally will not be able to get an elimination. Where Winston shines is disrupting backlines and creating openings for the rest of his team to follow up on his dives.

Heroes who can keep up with the speed of ![](/data/assets/guide/71e72edd3dddab12.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fjump-pack.png)Jump Pack are the best pairings. Think mobile burst damage heroes like ![](/data/assets/guide/c5e996565ab1a764.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fgenji.png)Genji, ![](/data/assets/guide/5c24a105db5a970e.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Ftracer.png)Tracer, and ![](/data/assets/guide/52c34367e459b0af.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fvendetta.png)Vendetta. Together, they can stomp the enemy backline.

For Supports, Winston needs high single-target healing so he can retreat, be healed, and get right back into the fight. Pairing Supports like ![](/data/assets/guide/3bd1f9f730a6a2ce.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fana.png)Ana or ![](/data/assets/guide/ca4458a60a9fff01.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fkiriko.png)Kiriko allow him to play aggressively, receive healing from a distance, and be saved by their utility cooldowns.

strengths.title: Extremely fast jump
content: Jump Pack sends ![](/data/assets/guide/55b5862f0bee17fa.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fwinston.png)Winston flying across the map and is one of the fastest movement abilities in OW. He uses the superior speed to catch enemies and force them into situations where they have to outplay him or die. Whether he’s taking high ground or jumping straight at the backline, the damage and speed of ![](/data/assets/guide/71e72edd3dddab12.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fjump-pack.png)Jump Pack are the core of ![](/data/assets/guide/55b5862f0bee17fa.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fwinston.png)Winston's kit.

strengths.title: Isolating enemies
content: ![](/data/assets/guide/55b5862f0bee17fa.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fheroes%2Fwinston.png)Winston excels at scouting and at jumping onto enemies who are separated from their team. On top of this, he also has ![](/data/assets/guide/3320e3b9cbd5d84c.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fbarrier-projector.png)Barrier Projector to completely cut enemies off from their team. Their team can’t shoot or heal through the barrier, which allows him and his team to quickly eliminate the isolated foe.

strengths.title: Barrier-piercing cleave
content: Other than melee attacks, ![](/data/assets/guide/6e13dbd3b63c0f90.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Ftesla-cannon.png)Tesla Cannon primary is the only attack that pierces barriers. The 12-second cooldown of ![](/data/assets/guide/3320e3b9cbd5d84c.png#fallback=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.mobalytics.gg%2Fcdn-cgi%2Fimage%2Fformat%3Dauto%2Cwidth%3D96%2Fassets%2Foverwatch%2Fimages%2Fabilities%2Fbarrier-projector.png)Barrier Projector is even more exploitable. The health usually lasts only a couple of seconds, leaving a long gap between Barrier uses.
